issues.issue: Did the RAD breach procedural fairness or show bias in assessing the two Congolese notices to appear?
issues.applicant_position: RAD was biased and relied on nonexistent evidence; it wrongly found differences between the copies and originals of identical notices.
issues.result_quote: Given the evidence before the RAD and the incomplete explanations provided by Ms. Munyandamusa, I cannot find anything unreasonable in this analysis.

issues.issue: Did the RAD apply the wrong standard of proof under s. 96 by discounting her Lucha membership as a political profile?
issues.applicant_position: Lucha membership itself can open the door to persecution for political opinion, even without participating in demonstrations.
issues.result_quote: It was open to the RAD to find that the political involvement entered into evidence did not establish that Ms. Munyandamusa had a well-founded prospective fear of persecution

issues.issue: Did the RAD have to give a s. 24 Rules notice before rejecting the notices on specialized knowledge?
issues.applicant_position: Rejecting the notices on specialized knowledge without a s. 24 notice breached procedural fairness (Abdelrahman, Torishta).
issues.result_quote: the failure to give a notice did not constitute a breach of the requirements of procedural fairness
